newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen shares tumble to close on crackdown fears.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares tumble to close on crackdown fears.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B share indices ended sharply lower on Wednesday on panic selling fuelled by apprehension over possible further action by Beijing to crack down on speculative trading, brokers said.
The A share index dived 11.71 points or 2.74 percent to close at 414.73 on turnover of 7.2 billion yuan against Tuesday's 6.0 billion yuan.
The B share index fell 4.75 points or 3.22 percent to 142.36 on turnover of HK$56.2 million compared with 108.9 million in the previous session.
Brokers said fears that Beijing was about to announce new anti-speculation policies sparked panic selling in A shares and pulled down their B share counterparts.
"Widespread crackdown-related rumours spooked investors who have been hard hit recently by a string of clampdown measures," an analyst with a foreign brokerage in Shenzhen said.
Rumours include Beijing planning to announce the punishment of several major domestic brokerages caught engaging in illicit stock trading, brokers said.
"The A share losses were created in part by selling from banks whose equity position liquidation deadline is drawing near," an analyst at J&A Securities (H.K.) Ltd said.
State banks are required to unwind their share positions within 10 sessions from last Friday to sqeeze the so-called "speculative bubble" out of the stock market.
"In view of recent measures, the central bank seems to be more determined than ever to bring down share prices," the J&A analyst said.
The short-term future of B shares is to follow the trend of the A share market, brokers said.
A technical rebound in the A and B share market is likely in the near future, though sentiment has been hit by today's sharp falls, they said.
On the B share market, Shenzhen Health Mineral Water was the worst performer, diving HK$0.31 or 8.75 percent to HK$3.23.
Paints producer Tianjin Beacon was the biggest loser in the A share market and dropped 0.93 yuan or 8.05 percent to 10.62 yuan.
